re_line: DPRK expels Swiss diplomat · KOSPI -6.16% on AI selloff · Cheonghae unit expanded · Chief Justice impeachment push · Russia Tu-160 near Ulleungdo
morning_memo: North Korea expelled the head of Switzerland's Pyongyang diplomatic office and demanded its closure within 48 hours over sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp.
KOSPI fell 6.16 percent to 4,697.51, reversing all of Tuesday's Jensen Huang-driven rally as Wall Street tech stocks sold off overnight.
President Lee reaffirmed the Cheonghae naval unit's operational zone will expand to the Arabian Sea south of Oman, with the Strait of Hormuz explicitly excluded.

key_stat.label: Annual public housing units Seoul plans to supply through 2030
key_stat.context: President Lee cited this figure at an Eunpyeong district housing event as the target annual supply rate, which he described as the highest on record.

imagery_report.label: Choe Hyon-class destroyer deployment and shipyard expansion
imagery_report.headline: Satellite imagery places Kang Kon at Mayang Island naval base, Choe Hyon at Nampo; Chongjin and Nampo shipyards expanding for additional large-warship construction
imagery_report.body: Daily NK Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed November 24 confirms North Korea's two 5,000-ton Choe Hyon-class destroyers have split between coasts: the Kang Kon is moored at the Mayang Island naval base and the Choe Hyon remains at Nampo. Shipyard expansion visible at both Chongjin and Nampo is consistent with construction of additional large warships.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after more than two years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12. Daily NK satellite imagery analyzed Nov 24 places the Kang Kon at Mayang Island naval base and the Choe Hyon at Nampo, with shipyard expansion visible at Chongjin and Nampo consistent with additional large-warship construction.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: NK News Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed through November 15, 2026 confirms trucks filling Sinuiju customs facility from October 16, the day after the New Yalu River Bridge officially opened, with activity peaking October 19–20. A wall of 40-foot containers bearing Maersk and COSCO markings was visible on the Chinese side. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reported November 18 that Sinuiju markets are overflowing with Chinese goods but a severe cash shortage means almost nobody is buying, with vendors describing a 'trading cliff.' Daily NK reported November 23 that low-income families in Sinuiju are sinking into crisis as market prices for food and daily necessities soar despite state promotion of Sinuiju development as a model for regional growth.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: Herald Economy reported November 23 that a North Korean vessel marked 'Marine Police' was spotted near Yeonpyeong Island, with the ROK Joint Chiefs confirming they are tracking and monitoring the vessel. As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20, 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14, 2026 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips. NK News reported November 24 that the Ukrainian military struck the cargo freighter Angara, one of the four vessels in the documented arms-transfer fleet, in a drone attack that also sank the Russian corvette Merkury.

top_stories.headline: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat, orders Pyongyang mission closed within 48 hours
top_stories.body: The DPRK Foreign Ministry's European Department director general **Pak Hyon Su** declared the head of Switzerland's Pyongyang diplomatic office, **Sylvain Astier**, persona non grata and ordered him to leave within 48 hours, citing Bern's sanctioning of the Songdowon International Children's Camp over its alleged role in transferring children from Russian-occupied Ukraine. Pak also submitted a memorandum demanding the closure of the office, which had opened only in October 2026. NK News analysis notes North Korea selectively targeted Switzerland and the United Kingdom while leaving EU member states that also sanctioned the camp unscathed.

top_stories.headline: Lee reaffirms Cheonghae unit expansion to Arabian Sea, bars Strait of Hormuz operations
top_stories.body: **Lee Jae-myung** reaffirmed that South Korea's Cheonghae naval unit will expand its operational zone from the Gulf of Aden to the open sea south of Oman, approximately *650 kilometers* from the Strait of Hormuz, after the National Assembly defense committee approved a revised dispatch motion. The unit will add maritime patrol aircraft and mine-clearing support to its existing destroyer role; the Strait of Hormuz and adjacent waters are explicitly excluded from the area of operations. Minor opposition parties have criticized the expansion as a backdoor troop dispatch to the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

top_stories.headline: KOSPI drops 6.16% as AI trade reverses; Democratic Party formally proposes five-party coalition to impeach Chief Justice
top_stories.body: South Korean shares fell *308.52 points*, or 6.16 percent, to close at 4,697.51 as an overnight Wall Street tech selloff erased the previous session's Jensen Huang-driven rally; Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell roughly 10 percent. Separately, Democratic Party leader **Kim Min-seok** formally proposed a five-party coalition with progressive parties to accelerate the impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice **Cho Hee-dae**, with the Changwon District Court issuing the first formal judicial statement of opposition, warning the push undermines constitutional separation of powers.

also_today.headline: NK Pro satellite imagery indicates DPRK tested ICBM engine last week as Trump sought Kim meeting at APEC
also_today.body_text: NK Pro analysis of satellite imagery suggests North Korea conducted a possible long-range missile static engine test around the time President Trump visited China and floated a meeting with Kim Jong Un at APEC in Shenzhen.

also_today.headline: Analysis: North Korea selectively targeted Switzerland and UK over children's camp sanctions, sparing EU member states
also_today.body_text: Three days after Kim Jong Un personally accepted credentials from ambassadors of 10 countries, Pyongyang expelled the Swiss mission head, a selective coercive move that leaves EU sanctioners unscathed, suggesting calibrated rather than blanket retaliation.

also_today.headline: Delta Air Lines backs Korean Air Chairman Cho Won-tae in Hanjin KAL ownership battle
also_today.body_text: Delta's vice president for Asia-Pacific said Delta, holding 14.9 percent of Hanjin KAL equity, is "highly confident" in Chairman **Cho Won-tae** as Hoban Group seeks to expand its influence over the airline conglomerate.

also_today.headline: Court documents reveal North Korean worker at Russian drone production factory arrested for theft
also_today.body_text: A Russian Far East court verdict in a theft case disclosed that the defendant was a North Korean worker employed at a drone manufacturing facility, the first documented instance placing a DPRK national inside a Russian weapons production plant.

also_today.headline: Trump says he could restart 'love letters' with Kim Jong Un immediately
also_today.body_text: President **Donald Trump** said he could resume the personal correspondence with Kim Jong Un that characterized his first term, days after the failed APEC summit meeting and amid NK Pro reporting of a possible DPRK ICBM engine test.

us_korea_deals.state_of_play: Steel and aluminum remain at 50 percent and autos at 15 percent, both under Section 232. The Section 122 surcharge expired July 24, so there is no baseline reciprocal tariff in force. Section 301 investigations, launched March 11 against 16 trading partners including South Korea, are now the primary vehicle for any new broad-based measure.

trade_policy.detail: Samsung received preliminary $6.4B CHIPS Act award (April 2024) for Taylor TX fabs; 10-year restriction on materially expanding semiconductor manufacturing in countries of concern; Samsung Xi'an NAND fab limited to legacy production.

business_economy.headline: Samsung Display takes 9.1% stake in ams OSRAM for 210 million euros to co-develop microLED
business_economy.body_text: Samsung Display will acquire 9.98 million newly issued shares at 21 euros each in European chipmaker ams OSRAM, becoming its largest shareholder, alongside a partnership to commercialize next-generation ultra-small microLED technology.

business_economy.headline: Aramco and S-OIL inaugurate $7 billion Shaheen petrochemical complex in South Korea
business_economy.body_text: Saudi Aramco and its South Korean subsidiary S-OIL inaugurated the Shaheen Project, the first commercial deployment of Aramco's proprietary thermal crude-to-chemicals technology, adding approximately *3.2 million tonnes* of annual petrochemical production capacity.

business_economy.headline: Korea Investment Savings Bank hack exposes personal data of 86,433 customers, largest breach in savings bank sector
business_economy.body_text: Korea Investment Savings Bank, a subsidiary of Korea Investment Financial Holdings, confirmed a cyberattack exposed names, phone numbers, passport numbers and account numbers of *86,433* customers, the largest data breach in the domestic savings bank industry.

business_economy.headline: National Assembly welfare subcommittee passes tiered basic pension reform, highest tier rising to 380,000 won
business_economy.body_text: The National Assembly's Health and Welfare Committee subcommittee passed an amendment to the Basic Pension Act dividing recipients into three income brackets, with the lowest-income elderly (bottom 30%) receiving 380,000 won per month, up 3,000 won from the current uniform rate.

northeast_asia.headline: Russian Tu-160 strategic bomber entered KADIZ near Ulleungdo; ROK defense ministry summoned Russian defense attaché
northeast_asia.body_text: Multiple Russian military aircraft, identified as Tu-160 supersonic strategic bombers capable of nuclear weapons delivery, entered South Korea's Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) without prior notice on November 24 and flew near Ulleungdo's airspace. ROK defense ministry international policy chief **Kim Hak-jo** summoned Russian defense attaché Colonel **Nikolai Marchenko** to lodge a formal protest and demand recurrence prevention.

northeast_asia.headline: Chinese ambassador in Seoul defends ties after opposition labels Lee 'pro-China'
northeast_asia.body_text: Chinese Ambassador **Dai Bing** publicly pushed back against criticism that President Lee Jae-myung is excessively pro-China, saying that good relations with a large neighbor is not disadvantageous, in direct response to People Power Party attacks on National Intelligence Service director-designate **Kang Keum-sil**'s advisory roles for Chinese local governments.

northeast_asia.headline: Draft recommendations for Japan's security document review reportedly include proposal to reconsider Three Non-Nuclear Principles
northeast_asia.body_text: An expert advisory panel reviewing Japan's three major security documents has included in a draft recommendation a proposal to revisit the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, which bar Japan from possessing, producing, or permitting entry of nuclear weapons, according to Yonhap's Tokyo bureau citing Japanese media.

rok_government.action: MND formally protests Russian military aircraft KADIZ violation near Ulleungdo
rok_government.detail: Multiple Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's KADIZ without prior notice on November 24 and flew near Ulleungdo's airspace; MND international policy chief Kim Hak-jo summoned Russian defense attaché Colonel Nikolai Marchenko to lodge a formal protest and demand recurrence prevention.

rok_government.action: 26-2nd Mugunghwa senior officers' conference held Nov 23-24
rok_government.detail: MND convened its second 2026 Mugunghwa Conference with more than 90 senior generals at Militopia Hotel by Marine, covering AI and drone technology education, autonomous defense promotion, and democracy and constitutional protection instruction.

rok_government.action: Repatriation ceremony held for Vietnam War KIA after 59 years
rok_government.detail: MND held a repatriation ceremony at Seoul Airport for the remains of Sergeant **An Gyu-tae**, killed in the Vietnam War, returned from Hawaii aboard a ROK Air Force C-130 transport.

calendar_watch.headline: KORAIL work-to-rule action begins
calendar_watch.detail: Korean Railway Workers' Union begins work-to-rule action at 9 a.m. Thursday, running through December 4, with an indefinite general strike threatened for December 10 if demands are unmet.

calendar_watch.headline: Justice Ministry committee to adopt Lee Yong-cheol confirmation report
calendar_watch.detail: The Democratic Party announced the National Assembly Legislation and Judiciary Committee will adopt the confirmation hearing report for Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol on November 27; People Power Party opposes adoption.

calendar_watch.headline: Supreme Court verdict on former first lady Kim Keon Hee's bribery case
calendar_watch.detail: The Supreme Court scheduled the final verdict in former first lady Kim Keon Hee's bribery case for next Thursday; both Kim and special counsel Min Joong-ki's team appealed an appellate ruling sentencing her to five years.

calendar_watch.headline: National judges' representative conference convenes
calendar_watch.detail: The National Judges' Representative Conference holds its second-half regular meeting at the Judicial Research and Training Institute in Goyang, with potential floor motions on the Supreme Court Chief Justice impeachment push and the 'judicial three laws' agenda.

calendar_watch.headline: National court presidents' conference scheduled
calendar_watch.detail: A national court presidents' conference is scheduled for December 4, where judicial independence and judicial self-examination are expected to be central topics amid the Democratic Party's push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae.

rok_assembly.action: Approves revised Cheonghae unit dispatch extension motion expanding operational zone to Arabian Sea
rok_assembly.detail: The defense committee's legislative subcommittee voted to approve a revised motion widening the Cheonghae unit's zone from the Gulf of Aden to the open sea south of Oman, adding maritime patrol aircraft and mine-clearing capability to the existing destroyer.

rok_assembly.action: Passes tiered basic pension amendment dividing recipients into three income brackets
rok_assembly.detail: The welfare subcommittee passed an amendment to the Basic Pension Act creating three income-tiered payment levels, with the lowest-income bracket (bottom 30%) receiving 380,000 won monthly, 3,000 won above the current uniform amount.

rok_assembly.action: DP-led review of four media reform bills begins over PPP objections
rok_assembly.detail: The culture committee's legislation subcommittee opened review of four media laws covering news agency, government advertising, newspapers, and press arbitration; PPP members walked out, calling the bills a 'shackle on the press.'

overnight_items.headline: Prosecutors summon ROK ambassador to China Ro Jae-hun over alleged Roh Tae-woo slush fund
overnight_items.body_text: Seoul Central District Prosecutors summoned sitting ambassador Ro Jae-hun as a suspect for questioning around end of November.

overnight_items.headline: PPP demands Lee withdraw NIS nominee Kang Keum-sil, citing China advisory roles
overnight_items.body_text: PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk labeled Kang 'pro-China, anti-American'; DP called the attack 'outdated McCarthyism.'

overnight_items.headline: Russia paid North Korea in fuel after Pyongyang rejected rupees for construction contract
overnight_items.body_text: DPRK demanded US dollars or Chinese yuan; Moscow offered Indian rupees before settling on fuel payment.

overnight_items.headline: Switzerland says it will maintain sanctions on Songdowon camp despite DPRK expulsion threat
overnight_items.body_text: Swiss government confirmed sanctions remain in effect as DPRK followed through and ordered the office closed.

overnight_items.headline: FT: North Korea closes Swiss diplomatic office in row over children's camp
overnight_items.body_text: Pyongyang described the Swiss sanctions as a 'blatant hostile act,' shuttering an office opened only weeks earlier.

overnight_items.headline: UK Treasury finds evidence of North Korea sanctions evasion links during investigation of suspect firms
overnight_items.body_text: British investigators found North Korea sanctions-evasion indicators during a probe of UK-registered suspicious entities.

rok_personnel.name: Oh Hyun-joo
rok_personnel.detail: FM Cho Hyun presided over the appointment ceremony for Oh Hyun-joo as KOICA's 15th president on November 25; she was formally appointed on November 16. The appointment was accompanied by a directive to strengthen KOICA's role as an integrated grant-aid platform.

social_statements.context: Rally in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province, Nov 25, on Chief Justice impeachment push
social_statements.analyst_note: PPP held the Gyeongju rally near Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae's hometown as part of a relay of regional outdoor rallies planned through November 29.

official_x_posts.analyst_note: Gen. Xavier Brunson's post highlights the Joint Security Area battalion's continuous presence at the Military Demarcation Line.

We have established the Korean Peninsula Peace Listening Corps under the minister and brought in civilian youth director Kim Hyo-joo to begin a civil-led, government-supported social dialogue.
official_x_posts.analyst_note: The ministry hosted its emerging researcher workshop on unification and North Korea studies the same day at Jeongdong 1928 Art Center.

opeds_today.headline: South Korea Cannot Police Its Way Out of AI Cheating
opeds_today.central_argument: South Korea's exam-centric education system faces a structural crisis from AI-enabled cheating that metal detectors and surveillance cannot solve, requiring fundamental reform of the high-stakes testing regime itself.
opeds_today.summary: The piece documents the top scorer on the tax exam confessing to AI cheating and 111 alleged AI-assisted cheating cases at this year's college entrance exam. It argues that South Korea's heavy reliance on standardized exams as gatekeepers for social mobility makes the country uniquely vulnerable to AI-enabled fraud. Policing measures treat the symptom while leaving the structural incentive for cheating, the exam system itself, intact.

opeds_today.headline: Japan, South Korea, US Are Taking Their Trilateral to the Arctic
opeds_today.central_argument: The US-ROK-Japan trilateral's extension into Arctic policy reflects a strategic logic of building shared interests in new domains beyond the established security-alliance framework centered on North Korea and China.
opeds_today.summary: The piece examines how the Camp David trilateral framework, originally focused on North Korea deterrence and China competition, is now extending into Arctic governance, shipping routes, and resource access. It assesses the rationale for bringing the Arctic into a peninsula-centered partnership as Russia's Arctic posture intensifies. The article raises the question of whether Arctic cooperation can generate durable momentum for the trilateral given historical frictions between Seoul and Tokyo.

opeds_today.headline: Making the Most of South Korea's Semiconductor Boom
opeds_today.central_argument: South Korea's semiconductor-driven economic gains carry systemic risk because the economy's growing dependence on a single global technology cycle leaves it exposed to AI demand volatility, a vulnerability the KOSPI's repeated circuit-breaker activations in 2026 illustrate.
opeds_today.summary: The piece argues that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have made South Korea an outsized beneficiary of the AI hardware boom but that concentration in one sector amplifies downside when sentiment shifts. It draws the connection between Korea's export dependency on advanced memory chips and the disproportionate KOSPI selloffs whenever Wall Street AI sentiment reverses. The author calls for industrial policy that diversifies the value chain rather than deepening semiconductor concentration.

top_articles.headline: Satellite images track North Korea's two new destroyers at opposite coasts
top_articles.summary: Daily NK Planet Labs imagery confirms the Kang Kon is moored at Mayang Island naval base and the Choe Hyon at Nampo, with shipyard expansion at Chongjin and Nampo consistent with additional large-warship construction.

kcna_delta.bottom_line: State media's dominant output Wednesday was the expulsion of Switzerland's Pyongyang mission head and the demand for the office's closure, while domestic content covered mushroom production and health unit achievements; KCNA remained silent on the failed Trump-Kim summit offer and NK Pro's reported ICBM engine test.

korea_world.headline: Korea-Oman FM talks: first Omani FM visit in 26 years covers energy, maritime security, shipbuilding
korea_world.body_text: FM Cho Hyun and Omani FM Al Busaidi discussed expanding cooperation from traditional energy trade, Oman is Korea's sixth-largest naphtha and seventh-largest LNG supplier, into maritime security, shipbuilding, port logistics, and renewable energy.
